item.title: Had I known, should you need, were it not for
item.explanation_text: In formal English, if can be dropped from a conditional and the auxiliary moved in front of the subject. Should + subject + bare infinitive replaces if for possible but unlikely future events, especially in formal letters and instructions: Should you require further information, please contact us. Were + subject + to-infinitive replaces if in hypothetical sentences: Were the university to raise its fees, many students would leave. With be, use were alone: Were I in your position, I would decline the offer. Had + subject + past participle replaces if in third and mixed conditionals: Had we left earlier, we would have caught the train. Were it not for (present) and Had it not been for (past) mean 'without': Were it not for her help, I would be lost. Had it not been for her help, I would have failed. In the negative, not comes after the subject and is never contracted: Had I not seen it (not Hadn't I seen it).
item.contrast_text: Compare: If I had known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi. Had I known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi. The meaning is the same; the second is more formal.
item.common_error_pattern: Keeping if together with inversion ('If had I known'), contracting the negative ('Hadn't I known'), or adding will after should ('Should you will need').

examples.bad: If had we booked earlier, we would have got a discount.
examples.good: Had we booked earlier, we would have got a discount.

examples.bad: Hadn't it been for the map, we would have got lost.
examples.good: Had it not been for the map, we would have got lost.

examples.bad: Should you will need help, call reception.
examples.good: Should you need help, call reception.

examples.bad: Were the university raise its fees, many students would leave.
examples.good: Were the university to raise its fees, many students would leave.

children.title: Correct the sentence
children.instructions: Find the mistake and write the whole sentence correctly.
children.prompt_text: If had I realised the meeting was cancelled, I wouldn't have driven to the office.
accepted_answers: Had I realised the meeting was cancelled, I wouldn't have driven to the office.
Had I realised the meeting was cancelled, I would not have driven to the office.
If I had realised the meeting was cancelled, I wouldn't have driven to the office.

children.prompt_text: Hadn't she warned us, we would have missed the deadline.
accepted_answers: Had she not warned us, we would have missed the deadline.
If she hadn't warned us, we would have missed the deadline.
If she had not warned us, we would have missed the deadline.
